title: While-You-Sleep Storefront — Customer Questionnaire
status: Replacement design; original founder questionnaire unrecovered

questions.prompt: What should shoppers come to your storefront to find?
options: Useful everyday finds with a distinctive look
questions.use: Sets the purpose of each edit, its product combinations, headlines and shopper benefit.

questions.prompt: Which categories belong in your storefront?
questions.use: Activates only the chosen category questions, sourcing and category-specific image tests.
questions.detail: These are starter categories, not a complete catalogue. Add any other category you want to curate; it needs its own brief and tests.

questions.prompt: How would you like to give us direction for each new edit?
options: Exact products or a detailed mock shopping list
Vibe photos: find products that fit the look
A guided theme brief: suggest products for my review
questions.use: Determines whether to preserve supplied products, interpret references, or propose a product shortlist. References are not permission to publish someone else’s images.
questions.detail: Optional: name the existing list or reference files. The operator retrieves and inspects them; missing files remain pending.

questions.prompt: Which visual styles should define your storefront?
questions.use: Directs product styling, scene density, surfaces, lighting and graphics together.
questions.detail: Optional: combine styles and say which leads. Include an existing approved example if you have one.

questions.prompt: Which palette and finishes should we use?
questions.use: Binds exact palette and material contrast to sourcing and all visual prompts.
questions.detail: Optional: name the dominant color, accent colors and colors/finishes to avoid. “Pink” alone does not mean a full pink room.

questions.prompt: Which personal details genuinely belong in your brand’s world?
questions.use: Provides meaningful contextual extras and activities; never adds every selected interest to every image.
questions.detail: If selected, specify the actual detail: for example the pet, flower, hobby or activity. Do not invent these from a broad checkbox.

questions.prompt: Which visual details should we exclude?
questions.use: Creates explicit image rejection rules. Product features and styling extras are distinguished; fixed product details need a recorded exception.
questions.detail: Optional: add particular flowers, surfaces, settings, motifs or other exclusions. A rejected example stays rejected.

questions.prompt: What should guide the products in each category you selected?
questions.use: Builds a separate shopper context, style/use brief and practical requirements for every selected category. Answer the category cards below.
questions.detail: Only selected categories appear. Each card uses choices, with optional precise requirements.

questions.prompt: Which shopping rules should we apply across your finds?
questions.use: Filters the product shortlist before generation, rather than trying to remove wrong items from finished images.
questions.detail: Name the material, ingredient, brand or product type when choosing “selected”. For category-specific exceptions, state the category.

questions.prompt: What shopping budget fits your audience?
options: Value matters more than one price ceiling
questions.use: Filters retail prices and total edit costs. This is the shopper budget, separate from image-generation spending.
questions.detail: For category limits, enter each category and ceiling. Optional: total outfit/room/gift budget and exceptions for investment pieces.

questions.prompt: Who should appear in lifestyle images?
options: Me, using my authorized reference images
No person: use the separately tested no-persona version
questions.use: Selects the identity/reference path or the distinct no-persona test. Never invents identity from written hair/age descriptions.
questions.detail: For a person, identify the existing reference file and confirm you have permission to use it. Do not ask again if these are already verified.

questions.prompt: Where would your persona naturally use or wear these finds?
options: Garden, porch or outdoor home spaces
questions.use: Produces plausible activities and different lifestyle viewpoints, rather than inserting a person into the styled image.
questions.detail: Optional: identify recurring real settings and activities. Skip this question for the no-persona path.

questions.prompt: How should your recommendations sound?
questions.use: Guides blog copy, titles, Pinterest descriptions and Instagram captions without inventing product claims.
questions.detail: Optional: approved phrases, words to avoid, and an existing writing sample.

questions.prompt: Which Amazon path do you actually have?
options: Not approved yet / still setting up
questions.use: Determines Idea List versus product-link handling and what can be completed. Approval is verified rather than inferred.
questions.detail: Optional: provide your owned storefront URL or existing account record. Never supply passwords here.

questions.prompt: Where should shoppers go from this content?
options: The exact Amazon Idea List for each edit
My own website page for each edit
My website plus the relevant Amazon destination
questions.use: Sets the destination chain and account ownership checks; never substitutes a storefront homepage for a missing per-edit link.
questions.detail: Identify existing owned URLs if available. Idea Lists require the Influencer path; website pages require a verified publishing path.

questions.prompt: Which outputs do you want included?
questions.use: Creates only requested channel assets, copy and publication checks. A channel choice is not publishing authorization.

questions.prompt: How do you want to operate the workflow?
options: Review first: prepare work, then I approve exact content and schedules
Automatic within a saved policy, only where supported and tested
Manual: I complete the steps using the prepared materials
Mixed: assign each step to me or the agent
questions.use: Sets ownership and approval boundaries for sourcing, generation, links, website and scheduling.
questions.detail: For mixed mode, assign those steps explicitly. Unsupported automatic steps are blocked, not silently handed back to you.

questions.prompt: Which image-generation route do you want to use?
options: Help me compare routes before choosing
questions.use: Selects a route to verify for actual model, references, output settings and cost. No automatic provider switch.
questions.detail: No subscription or paid generation is authorized by this selection. Exact capabilities and cost must be verified separately.

questions.prompt: Should we use an existing posting plan or configure a new one?
options: Use my existing confirmed posting plan
questions.use: Loads the recorded look count, channel-specific output count, spacing, dates and seasonal calendar. A saved plan is carried forward without asking again.
questions.detail: Show this question only when the plan is missing or the client explicitly wants to change it. For a new plan, configure actual counts, days, times and spacing against the selected channels and verified capacity. No invented frequency tiers. The operator retrieves existing schedules and reconciles them before any change.

questions.prompt: Which timezone should control your schedule?
questions.use: Controls scheduling and recovery timestamps; never uses the operator computer’s timezone.
questions.detail: For another timezone, give a city or timezone name.

questions.prompt: What image-generation spending are you authorizing?
questions.use: Creates an enforceable spending and retry ceiling before any submission, including failed and uncertain attempts.
questions.detail: For a paid allowance: enter amount, unit/currency, per-look ceiling and period ceiling. For every route: enter maximum attempts per image role, including corrections. Missing numbers block generation.

operator_checks: Retrieve existing answers first; preserve exact source, timestamps and revision. Ask only for missing/conflicting preferences.
Verify asset rights, actual references and persona identity inputs.
Verify Amazon path, affiliate attribution, exact destinations and disclosure.
Verify owned accounts, board IDs/visibility, channel permissions and publisher readback.
Verify provider/model, reference support, actual cost and finite budget.
Verify durable profile write/readback, schedule capacity, paused task payloads and resume behavior.
Compile answer application for sourcing and all nine workflow steps; no unanswered field may be defaulted.
Run one inspected BASIC → STYLED → LIFESTYLE mini test per selected category and selected buyer path before scaling. Reject actual defects; preserve failures.
Keep publication and customer release subject to separate live evidence and authorization.
answer_contract: Persist each exact answer immediately in the same private profile, with question ID, question version, source, timestamp, revision and readback. Record a new answer as new; do not label it recovered. Corrections retain history and invalidate affected prepared inputs/tests.

custom_category_branch.prompt: Who are these products for, and how will they use them?
Which product types, functions and styles should lead?
Which fit, compatibility, material, care or other requirements matter? Write “No additional requirements” if none.
